metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling to join Steelers
metadata.description: Marquez Valdes-Scantling is expected to sign to the Steelers' practice squad.
metadata.analysis: After being let go by the Chargers this past weekend, Valdes-Scantling will meet back up with QB Aaron Rodgers and other familiar faces in Pittsburgh. Valdes-Scantling played in five games with the Steelers last season, catching 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling - Set to sign with Pittsburgh
metadata.description: The Steelers are planning to sign Valdes-Scantling to the practice squad, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reported Monday.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling is expected to start on the practice squad and work his way up to playing with former teammate Aaron Rodgers on the active roster. The wide receiver contributed 690 receiving yards and six touchdowns to Rodgers' 2020 MVP campaign and 430 yards and three touchdowns to his 2021 MVP campaign, both with the Packers.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling to Join Steelers' Practice Squad
metadata.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers are planning to sign veteran free-agent wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad. The veteran wideout is expected to begin on the practice squad and work his way onto the active roster. The 32-year-old hasn't done much lately, with 142 total receiving yards over the last two seasons combined. This is noteworthy because Valdes-Scantling and quarterback Aaron Rodgers played together in Green Bay earlier in their careers. They may recreate some of that magic in Pittsburgh. The Steelers are in desperate need of wide receivers right now, so it might not take him too long before he joins the active roster.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling - Dropped by Los Angeles
metadata.description: The Chargers released Valdes-Scantling on Saturday.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling linked up with the Chargers in mid-September and got into three games with the club, catching two of five targets for 22 yards. Los Angeles activated KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) from IR on Saturday, and Valdes-Scantling was the corresponding roster cut. The veteran wideout may now seek out an opportunity with another NFL organization in need of wide-receiver depth.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) set to play Sunday
metadata.description: Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) is set to play in Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling is now off of the injury report after being limited at practice earlier in the week with a rib issue. He will play in Week 6 but doesn't project to make a big impact for the Chargers for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) upgraded to full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday due to a rib injury. He should play in Week 6 and will see more work than usual with the high number of injuries that Los Angeles is dealing with to their wideouts right now.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling - Upgraded to full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Valdes-Scantling (ribs) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling was limited Wednesday, though his full participation Thursday suggests he will be good to go Sunday versus the Chiefs. The 32-year-old has appeared in three games for Los Angeles in 2026, catching two passes (five targets) for 22 yards.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wasn't able to log a full practice on Wednesday, as he was left limited by a rib issue of some kind. He remains off of the fantasy radar moving forward, regardless of his injury status heading into Week 6.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling - Limited with rib issue
metadata.description: Valdes-Scantling (ribs) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling is dealing with a rib injury that he likely suffered during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. The wide receiver was not given an official injury designation and has already practiced in a limited fashion during the first prep session of Week 6. This indicates that Valdes-Scantling is dealing with a minor injury and will likely be able to suit up for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling a Deep-League Waiver Option
metadata.description: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling could see another substantial snap share in Week 6 against the Kansas City Chiefs, although his fantasy appeal remains limited to deeper leagues. With Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) sidelined, Ladd McConkey (foot) available only for emergencies, and Tre' Harris (hamstring) exiting early, Valdes-Scantling played 75% of the offensive snaps in Sunday's 23-17 loss to Denver. Despite the expanded playing time, he caught just two passes for 22 yards on three targets and has only five targets across three appearances this season. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh indicated Monday that McConkey could begin working back into the mix this week, while Johnston may remain limited in practice. Valdes-Scantling could continue seeing significant playing time if those injuries persist, but his lack of targets makes him difficult to trust in fantasy lineups. Managers in leagues with 14 or more teams can consider him for temporary receiver depth, although there's little incentive to invest heavily in a player who could see his opportunities disappear once the Chargers get healthier. Los Angeles also has a Week 7 bye approaching.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling sees one target in Week 3
metadata.description: Marquez Valdes-Scantling failed to catch his only target in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling saw minimal involvement in the passing attack after being added to the active roster earlier in the week, finishing last on the team in targets. The veteran wideout can remain off rosters in all formats, with a Week 4 contest against the Seattle Seahawks up next.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling - Signed to active roster
metadata.description: Valdes-Scantling was signed to the Chargers' active roster Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling inked a deal to join the practice squad with Los Angeles on Sept. 15, and he will now get a shot with the active roster. The 31-year-old will provide the team with another veteran option at wide receiver ahead of Week 3 versus the Bills.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling signing with Chargers 53-man roster
metadata.description: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said they're signing WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling to the 53-man roster.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling will hold a depth role. He will remain off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling signs with Chargers
metadata.description: The Chargers signed wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling to the practice squad.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling had a successful workout on Tuesday. It is unclear if this relates to the injury for Ladd McConkey.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling - Joins Chargers' practice squad
metadata.description: The Chargers signed Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad Tuesday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling spent training camp with the Cowboys but was released on cutdown day. Valdes-Scantling has ample NFL experience, though his numbers have dwindled since he recorded 687 receiving yards with Kansas City in 2022. Valdes-Scantling's signing may have been in response to top Chargers wideout Ladd McConkey being day-to-day due to a rib injury. With that said, Valdes-Scantling isn't likely to make a major fantasy impact at this point in his career even if he logs some time on the gameday roster.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling works out for Chargers
metadata.description: The Chargers hosted WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling for a workout on Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling was released by the Cowboys at the end of training camp.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling Signing with Chargers
metadata.description: According to Jeremy Fowler, the Los Angeles Chargers are signing wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad on Tuesday. The veteran wideout was with the Dallas Cowboys during training camp, but he didn't make the final roster. He has bounced around the league in the past few seasons, but he could still provide depth to this roster. The Chargers could need another wideout with Ladd McConkey (rib) considered day-to-day right now. If he misses Week 2, Valdes-Scantling could be elevated to the active roster, but it's unlikely he'd do much during his first week with the organization. Fantasy managers can ignore MVS for the moment.

metadata.title: Chargers Working Out Marquez Valdes-Scantling Amid WR Injuries
metadata.description: The Los Angeles Chargers are working out free-agent veteran wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling on Tuesday, sources told Jordan Schultz. The two-time Super Bowl champion was with the Dallas Cowboys during training camp this summer before being released, and he has 219 catches, 3,686 receiving yards, and 21 touchdowns in his eight-year NFL career. He played in 10 games (one start) last year with the San Francisco 49ers and Pittsburgh Steelers and caught 14 of his 29 targets for only 120 yards and one touchdown. The Chargers are seeking a little more WR depth going into their Week 2 divisional tilt against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday after top wideout Ladd McConkey (rib) suffered a rib injury that has him listed as day-to-day this week. Additionally, Keandre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) is expected to miss some time after getting hurt in the Week 1 season-opening loss to the Arizona Cardinals. The Chargers' top wideouts this Sunday will likely be Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris if McConkey is not cleared to suit up.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling released by Cowboys
metadata.description: The Cowboys released Marquez Valdes-Scantling.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling signed a one-year deal with the Cowboys this offseason. He will seek a depth role with another team.

metadata.title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling - Cut by Cowboys
metadata.description: Valdes-Scantling was released by the Cowboys on Sunday, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
metadata.analysis: Valdes-Scantling was unable to secure a depth role in Dallas' top-heavy wide receiver room. With 116 games of regular-season NFL experience under his belt, plus 12 playoff contests, MVS could appeal to another team in search of a veteran presence that can stretch the field at wide receiver.
